_readme: What each data source allows, read by Polite (harvest/Gagame.Harvest/Core/Polite.cs) on every fetch; the schema is docs/FIDELITY.md section 2. A source's numbers are its OWN only where stated is true and documented names the page; every other number is ours and conservative. A host takes the most specific entry whose hosts list matches it (equal, or a subdomain; a pattern ending in '.' matches anywhere in host + '.'), else the default. Researched 2026-10-13. Override the path with GAGAME_SOURCE_LIMITS.

noaa.coops.api.title: NOAA CO-OPS Data API and Metadata API
noaa.coops.api.maxSpan: 1-minute 4 days; 6-minute 1 month; hourly and high/low 1 year; daily means 10 years; monthly means 200 years; high/low predictions 10 years, other predictions 1 year; currents 1 month, all bins 7 days, max/slack predictions 1 year
noaa.coops.api.quote: Data length is limited to 1 month
noaa.coops.api.note: The span per request is stated; the rate is not: the page says queries from one customer are throttled and asks for sleeps between calls, with no number. The Metadata API page (https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/mdapi/prod/) states no limit.

noaa.coops.web.title: NOAA Tides and Currents web pages
noaa.coops.web.note: Not researched beyond the API page; the default pace applies.

noaa.ndbc.title: NOAA National Data Buoy Center realtime files
noaa.ndbc.quote: We ask that you limit your retrievals to a minimal level.
noaa.ndbc.note: A request for restraint without a number; most stations report hourly, about 25 minutes after the hour.

ncep.nomads.title: NCEP NOMADS and the NCEP ftp web services
ncep.nomads.quote: restrict individual user access to 120 hits/minute
ncep.nomads.note: Service Change Notice 21-32 (effective 2021-04-20): the 120 is summed per IP over all the hosts listed, so they share one pace here. 2.5 s is ours (Polite's before this file), slower than the stated 0.5 s.

aws.s3.title: Amazon S3: the NOAA Open Data Dissemination buckets (noaa-*-pds), USGS TNM, Overture
aws.s3.quote: 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned Amazon S3 prefix
aws.s3.note: The stated number is S3's capacity per prefix, not a politeness policy; the registry pages (https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-coastal-lidar/) state no usage limit and no account is needed. The pace here is the default.

aws.registry.title: Registry of Open Data on AWS (pages)

noaa.ncei.title: NOAA NCEI (THREDDS, ETOPO, CUDEM, GSHHG)
noaa.ncei.note: A search for an NCEI THREDDS or download rate policy found none (2026-10-13); other THREDDS operators throttle per IP, so the default pace applies.

noaa.ofs.thredds.title: NOAA Operational Forecast Systems on THREDDS / OPeNDAP
noaa.ofs.thredds.note: Not found; the same model files are also on S3 (noaa-nos-ofs-pds).

usgs.waterservices.title: USGS Water Services (legacy NWIS web services)
usgs.waterservices.note: No rate stated. USGS announced the service is decommissioned in the first quarter of 2027, with intentional degradation possible from August 2026 (https://waterdata.usgs.gov/blog/api-waterservices-decom/).

usgs.waterdata.api.title: USGS Water Data APIs (OGC API)
usgs.waterdata.api.quote: you can make more requests per hour before getting rate limited
usgs.waterdata.api.note: Rate-limited per hour, higher with a free key; the number is not on the page but in each response's X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining headers (the page's example shows 1000).

usgs.api.water.title: USGS api.water.usgs.gov: the Network-Linked Data Index (NLDI) and the wmadata GeoServer (NHDPlus V2 flowlines, WFS)
usgs.api.water.note: No limit on a page; the host sits behind api-umbrella and every response carries X-Ratelimit-Limit: 3600 (an hour, no key; seen 2026-10-21). 1.5 s is ours, under the header's one a second. compose-river reads the NHDPlus terminals, level paths, upstream-main gauges and station flowlines here.

erddap.coastwatch.title: NOAA CoastWatch West ERDDAP (NMFS SWFSC ERD) and its mirror upwell
erddap.coastwatch.quote: run just one script or curl command at a time
erddap.coastwatch.note: A request for one request in flight (Polite's own law), no number; the tabledap documentation page says the same. griddap: a very large request 'will usually fail', so the bed asks one 1 degree chunk at a time. upwell answers metadata itself but redirects data requests (302) to coastwatch.pfeg; both are one source here. Checked 2026-10-14.

erddap.marine-ie.title: Marine Institute (Ireland) ERDDAP
erddap.marine-ie.quote: run just one script or curl command at a time
erddap.marine-ie.note: The stock ERDDAP request for one request in flight, no number. The Irish Weather Buoy Network is CC BY 4.0 (the dataset's license attribute). Checked 2026-10-14.

copernicus.marine.title: Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS)
copernicus.marine.note: Needs an account. A search summary of the help pages reports an 800 MB limit per web-GUI subset and none for the Toolbox; not confirmed on a fetched page, so not taken as stated. No harvester fetches from it today.

osm.overpass.title: Overpass API (main public instance)
osm.overpass.quote: a maximum of about 10000 requests per day
osm.overpass.note: And downloads below about 1 GB a day. No harvester queries Overpass today.

osm.planet.title: OpenStreetMap planet files and extracts (planet.openstreetmap.org, Geofabrik, osmdata)
osm.planet.note: No limit stated on the planet page or Geofabrik's technical page (https://download.geofabrik.de/technical.html); the planet page points at extracts and torrents for the large files.

gebco.title: GEBCO global grid
gebco.note: Public domain; no download limit stated.

noaa.enc.title: NOAA Electronic Navigational Charts (ENC Direct, charts.noaa.gov)

overture.title: Overture Maps releases (STAC; the data on S3 overturemaps-us-west-2)
overture.note: No limit stated; the S3 copy falls under aws.s3.

google.title: Google Maps Platform (Map Tiles API and every Google host)
google.quote: Maximum 10,000 root tileset queries per day.
google.note: Banned for harvesters (the engine's own day ledger, core/DayLedger.h, governs the Google tile source). Stated default quotas: 3D tiles 10,000 root tileset queries a day and 12,000 renderer queries a minute; 2D and Street View tiles 6,000 a minute and 15,000 a day per project; subject to change.
